paraphrase: Bondage is not due to avidyā, for what is unreal cannot bind; if avidyā were real, non-dualism would be abandoned. 'We are not six-category theorists like the Vaiśeṣikas', yet what is irrational is not accepted.

paraphrase: Against the view that all is momentary: recognition (of the same thing) contradicts it; it conflicts with scripture and reason; there can be no cause–effect relation between things arising at the same moment, or when the earlier has perished before the later arises.

paraphrase: Things are not mere consciousness, since external objects are cognized; the view that reality is empty and that being perishes is 'mere slander by the unawakened', and on either view there would be no human goal.
speaker: Kapila (traditional ascription)

paraphrase: The conjunction (of puruṣa with prakṛti) is due to non-discrimination; it is removed by its definite cause (discrimination) as darkness (by light); when non-discrimination about pradhāna goes, the other non-discriminations go too.

paraphrase: Prakṛti is the equilibrium of sattva, rajas and tamas; from prakṛti comes mahat, from mahat ahaṃkāra, from ahaṃkāra the five subtle elements and both (kinds of) organs, from the subtle elements the gross elements; and puruṣa: this is the group of twenty-five.

paraphrase: The principles are inferred in reverse order: the subtle elements from the gross, ahaṃkāra from these, the internal instrument from that, prakṛti from that; puruṣa because aggregates are for another. The root has no root: the rootless root.

paraphrase: Valid cognition is the ascertainment of an object not already known; its most effective means is threefold. Perception is the cognition that, being in contact, reflects the form of its object.

paraphrase: Īśvara is not established, since he could be neither free nor bound: either way he could not create. Scriptural mentions are praise of a liberated self or of an accomplished (yogin), for worship. speaker: Kapila (traditional ascription)
notes: Numbering per the Sansknet e-text; other recensions may differ by a sūtra or so.

paraphrase: Pradhāna acts for the liberation of the (ever-)free (puruṣa) or for its own sake; liberation is not attained by mere hearing, because beginningless latent tendencies are strong; agency is real in prakṛti and superimposed on puruṣa.
speaker: Kapila (traditional ascription)

paraphrase: The organs are not elemental, since scripture speaks of them as arising from ahaṃkāra.

paraphrase: The shared function of the instruments is the five winds; the functions of the organs are gradual and non-gradual; the modifications are fivefold, afflicted and unafflicted; when they cease, (puruṣa), its coloring calmed, abides in itself, like a crystal (when the flower is removed).

paraphrase: Consciousness is not natural to the body, since it is not seen in the elements separately; (objection:) it may arise from their combination like intoxicating power (from ingredients) — (answered in the sequel).

paraphrase: Liberation comes from knowledge, bondage from error; since (knowledge) is the fixed cause, there is neither combination (with works) nor option.

paraphrase: Meditation (dhyāna) is the removal of passion; it is accomplished through the cessation of mental modifications.

paraphrase: It is accomplished by concentration, posture and one's own duty; restraint (of breath) by expulsion and retention; posture is what is steady and pleasant; one's own duty is performing the acts enjoined for one's stage of life; (it is accomplished) also by dispassion and practice.

paraphrase: Fulfilment does not come from absorption into the cause, for one rises again, like one who has dived.

paraphrase: Even without being (a creator), one (absorbed in prakṛti) becomes connected (with creation again) through dependence; for he becomes all-knowing and all-doing; the establishment of such a lord is accepted.

paraphrase: Pradhāna's creation is for another, like a camel carrying saffron; though unconscious, its activity is like that of milk; or like karma or time; spontaneous, like a servant's; or drawn on by beginningless karma.

paraphrase: On discriminative knowledge pradhāna's creation ceases, like a cook's when the cooking is done; liberation is the indifference of one of the two.

paraphrase: The fruit of action is not governed by Īśvara, since it is accomplished by karma; a governor acts for his own benefit like a worldly lord; not without passion; with it he would not be eternally free; there is no means of knowledge for him and no inference, for want of a relation; and scripture speaks of (the world) as pradhāna's product.

paraphrase: Error is not the appearance of the non-existent, nor of the existent, nor of the indescribable, nor appearance-as-other (which is self-contradictory); it is the appearance of the existent-and-non-existent, since it is both sublated and not sublated.

paraphrase: There is no non-duality of the self, since difference is known from marks; nor of self with non-self. Neither self nor avidyā is the material cause of the world.
